speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
text: asked Minister for Education (a) given the shift back to Phase Two (Heightened Alert), what is the assessed risk level for children under the age of 12 who are unable to be vaccinated; and (b) what are the considerations when deciding the further steps that need to be taken, particularly in indoor educational settings, to ensure the safety of these children and their families, whether now or in the future when moving into COVID-19 as an endemic disease.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: To keep our children safe in the school environment, we implement stringent safe management and surveillance measures, and have adjusted the conduct of school activities where necessary.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: All staff in schools and preschools are required to wear masks.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Students in school are also required to wear masks, while in preschools, either masks or face shields are strongly encouraged for children above the age of two.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: For mask-off activities in schools, extra safe management measures are taken.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: For example, physical education classes are conducted outdoors or in well-ventilated venues and in small groups based on national guidelines.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Preschools and schools also emphasise good personal hygiene and social responsibility.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Staff in preschools and schools are also prioritised for vaccination.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: These measures collectively mitigate the risks of infection in our students.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Ultimately, managing COVID-19, whether nationally or in our school setting, is about managing risks and balancing trade-offs.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Over time, we have developed a better understanding of the virus and how to live with it in our daily lives.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: As we move towards a new normal of COVID-19 as an endemic disease, we are making a conscious move to adopt an appropriate risk management strategy and collectively determine what level of risk is acceptable to us as a society.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: The past few months have given us more confidence that we can strike a better balance by taking a more targeted approach to ring-fence cases and their close contacts.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: For example, by only having affected classes, levels or schools on Home-Based Learning (HBL), rather than resorting to full HBL for everyone on a nationwide scale.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: This has allowed us to isolate affected students and staff, and not close all Primary schools, where most students are not yet eligible for vaccination.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: The alternative of full HBL on a prolonged basis comes at the cost of the learning and especially the social-emotional development of our young.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: And it takes a toll on the mental wellness, places additional stresses on educators, parents and students, especially when not all students have home environments that are conducive for HBL.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: The negative impact also falls disproportionally on lower-income families.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We will continue to finetune how we manage school cases and ensure its sustainability as we transit towards living with COVID-19 as an endemic disease.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Taking reference from the national posture and working closely with parents, we will continue to work hard to keep our schools and students safe.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: The reason I asked this question is because a lot of parents have come to me and said they are worried about the health and safety of their children, especially those under the age of 12, who are unable to get vaccinated at the moment.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: I just wanted to ask what efforts are being made to address these concerns, as in efforts to address these parents directly?

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: Because, obviously, a lot of them are very worried, a lot of them are writing to me and writing to all of us here.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: They want to know how about those parents, for example, with children who have pre-existing medical conditions that make these children more vulnerable, if they do actually get COVID-19.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: Are these children expected to isolate or stay at home?

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: What are the actual effects this will actually have on these children?

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: These are some of the questions that parents have come up to me with and I would just like some clarifications from the Minister about this.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: Earlier, the Minister also said that the task force is studying the safety of vaccinations on children under the age of 12.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: Do we have any estimates of when we expect to see results because the Minister mentioned that more announcements and decisions will be made at the appropriate time?

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: Do we have an estimate of when this is expected to be available?

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: Lastly, I just wanted to ask, especially at the preschools and maybe even infant care levels, as many parents with young children will know, it is actually very difficult for these children to keep their masks on and adhere to hygiene and safe distancing measures.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: What sort of extra steps and precautions are taken to make sure that these children and by definition, their family members, especially vulnerable family members at home are also protected?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: But as far as we know, the work has started to trial this, to see if it is appropriate for children below the age of 12.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Having said that, what we need to do is to make sure that we put in place the safe management measures for our children to live their life as normally as possible so that they can continue to grow up and continue learning as much as possible.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We need to do this in a sustainable way; and I want to emphasise this: "sustainable way".

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We do not know how long this disease will continue to ravage the world.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We do not know when the vaccine will come.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Bearing this in mind, we need sustainable solutions in order to allow our children, especially those below the age of 12, to continue learning and growing in as normal an environment as possible.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: As I have mentioned in my speech, what are some of the things that we can do?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Having said that, it does not mean that those people who are vaccinated are no longer going to transmit or be carriers of the virus.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: But what it does mean is that the chances are reduced and the symptoms are much less.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: That is also one way to keep our younger children safe.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Beyond that preventive step, we are looking at the next step which we have also done: to make sure that we organise our activities in such a way that can allow our children to interact, learn in a group, but not having too many of them mixing around and just in case anything happens, which means that we have tight cohorting in the schools, preschools, to minimise the chances of this happening.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The next ring that we must implement is that upon the detection of any of the cases, quickly ring-fence the affected parties so that we can minimise the chances of this spreading to the rest.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: This is where parents can also play a part to work with the schools and the preschools to keep our children safe.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: If, for whatever reasons, a member of the family is ill, please do not send the children to school until we have verified that the children or the family will not pose a risk to the other students in the school.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: So, I think, collectively, we can also do that.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: But at this point in time, we do not yet have that less intrusive testing capability for the younger ones.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: So, we have to continue to work together to make sure that we keep our children and our schools safe.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: But coming back to that, I would like to appeal to everyone that we need to make this work on a sustainable basis.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And that is why we need to work together.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We can do certain things in the short term, we can scale up certain measures but the question is how do we make such measures sustainable, bearing in mind the interests of the children, the families and also the educators, which was what I had explained to the public last Friday.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The last question Ms He Ting Ru asked about was infant care and the preschool.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Indeed, we all understand it is harder for the children of the younger ages to keep their masks on and it will take extra effort for us to make sure that we apply the safe management measures, keeping their personal hygiene good and, at the same time, cohorting them to minimise the chances of transmission, in case something should happen, in case one of them should be infected with this.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Having said that, it is very important for everyone again to work together so that a child who is sick or a child who is from a family who has someone ill and not verified yet, to avoid sending the child to the school or the preschool so that we minimise the chances of this spreading to other people.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And we would need everybody's cooperation to make this happen.
